evidence.note: Ran test.sh and iterated to pass on visible inputs (repetitive/simple); progress gauged by whether individual sample inputs decode, not by an explicit coverage map — conflates 'sample passes' with progress.

~35 consecutive apply-patch/make/run cycles all against the single audio.wav.zst input. Shows awareness of being stuck on one input, but tunnel-visioned on it for the entire back half without returning to verify the broader feature matrix.

During the audio debugging the agent switched diagnostic tactics rather than retrying one fix: re-read an RFC clause (45), grepped FSE decode code (83), and took targeted hex dumps at specific offsets (99/102/103) — genuine re-diagnosis, though only after many repeated cycles, not early.

Trajectory ends with more patches and a git diff; no final broad verification across untested feature classes (dictionaries, multi-frame, skippable, treeless, 4-stream), so claimed-done is never reconciled against verified-done.

reasoning: The agent tracks progress implicitly via sample-input decoding rather than an explicit coverage map, and never verifies large feature classes (dictionaries, multi-frame, treeless) — weaker than the level-8 'explicit accurate coverage map.' However, it clearly notices repeated failure on the same input (audio.wav.zst) and does switch diagnostic tactics (hex-level traces, RFC re-read, code grep) rather than looping on one fix, which is above the level-3 'little awareness of being stuck.' The combination — notices being stuck and re-diagnoses, but keeps only a rough/implicit sense of coverage and tunnel-visions on one input — lands squarely at the level-5 anchor.
